summary: You can trample farmland in spawn protection
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Start a server.
2. Join the server and give yourself operator permissions.
3. Switch to Creative mode.
4. Set the world spawn at your current location with `/setworldspawn ~ ~ ~`.
5. Place water nearby with `/setblock ~1 ~-1 ~-2 minecraft:water`.
6. Place farmland nearby with `/setblock ~ ~-1 ~-2 minecraft:farmland`.
7. Switch to Survival mode and remove your operator permissions.
8. Have another player retain or receive operator permissions to activate spawn protection.
9. Jump on the farmland.
10. Observe that the farmland is trampled inside spawn protection.
Observed Behavior:
A non-operator player in Survival mode can trample farmland located within the server’s spawn-protection area by jumping on it. The farmland changes into dirt even though the same player cannot normally place, break, or interact with protected blocks.

This occurs because the farmland trampling logic runs when an entity lands on the block without checking whether the entity is permitted to interact with the farmland under spawn-protection rules.
Expected Behavior: Players without operator permissions should be unable to trample or otherwise alter farmland located within spawn protection. When a non-operator jumps on protected farmland, the block should remain farmland rather than being converted to dirt, consistent with the restriction preventing them from interacting with or destroying protected blocks. Farmland outside spawn protection should retain its normal trampling behavior.
